name: Mini Christmas Pop-Tart Cookies
desc: Bite-size pie dough pop tarts filled with homemade cranberry-raspberry jam and dipped in pink glaze.

source.title: Mini Christmas Pop-Tart Cookies
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 1 (14.1 oz) box refrigerated roll-out pie dough (2 crusts)
1 large egg beaten with 2 tbsp water, for egg wash
ingredients.prep: beaten with 2 tbsp water, for egg wash

ingredients.raw: 1/2-1 tsp cranberry-raspberry jam (or food coloring), to tint

steps: Jam: in a 3 qt saucepan over medium heat, bring the cranberries, raspberries, sugar and 1 tbsp water to a simmer. Simmer 7-10 min, until the cranberries have popped.
Blend on high until smooth. Press through a fine-mesh sieve in small batches with a spatula and discard the seeds and skins.
Stir the cornstarch into the 1 1/2 tbsp water, stir it into the puree, and heat in the saucepan over medium-low until it bubbles and thickens, a few minutes. Cool completely. You will have extra jam.

Cookies: heat the oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment. On floured parchment, roll one crust from about 10 in to about 14 in across and trim it to a rectangle, saving the scraps. Roll the second crust the same way.
Spoon or pipe a heaping teaspoon of jam onto each cookie spot on the first sheet of dough (ravioli stamp squares or marked squares). Brush egg wash on all the seams between them.

Lay the second crust on top, press around each mound, and cut with a ravioli stamp, fluted pastry wheel or knife. If you cut with a knife, crimp the edges with a fork. Pinch any edge that shows a gap.
Set 12 cookies per sheet. Press the scraps together, re-roll to the same thickness, and repeat.
Brush the tops lightly with egg wash. Bake 12-15 min, until lightly golden. Cool completely on a rack.
Glaze: stir the powdered sugar, corn syrup and salt with the water added a little at a time until smooth and thick but dippable. Tint pink with the jam.

Set a wire rack over parchment. Dip the top of each cookie, shake off the excess, and set it on the rack. For an opaque finish, let the first coat set 15-20 min and dip again. Add sprinkles while the last coat is still wet.
Let dry several hours, until the glaze hardens, before stacking. Store airtight.
tips: Egg wash on the seams is what stops the jam leaking.
Double dip because the glaze soaks in and dries thinner. For a single dip, halve the glaze.
The assembled cookies freeze well unbaked. Thaw to room temperature before baking.
Her brown sugar cinnamon version uses a filling of dark brown sugar, cinnamon, flour, apple butter, oil and salt, sealed with water.
